answer: For orchard monitoring, propose one paid key per surveyed terrace of at least one hectare, leased exclusively for 60 days. Its calibrated sensor signs a spray plume trace; independent inspectors audit sites in a surprise shared window. Validators deny pay on a duplicated plot ID or missing trace and forfeit that key's escrow on a proven forged reading. A farm's cheapest move is a shared model and leased land; each clone still costs one separate hectare, live sensor and 60-day lease. Borrowed cash cannot make one plot serve two keys. These are new rules, not MinePoA policy.
